claims.statement: A note is a repo-relative markdown file consisting of an optional YAML frontmatter block plus a body: `frontmatter_gate.split_frontmatter()` splits the two and they reconstruct the file exactly as "---\n" + fm + "---\n" + body. A note with no frontmatter accepts a body replacement, but asking to set or delete frontmatter fields on it raises ValueError("no frontmatter to edit") rather than implicitly creating a block.

A note's display identity resolves through one fixed precedence chain in `ingest.note_title()` — frontmatter `title:`, then the first level-1 ATX heading, then the de-kebabbed path stem with a leading ISO date stripped — and `ingest.doc_surface()` builds the doc-lane text from that title plus all headings plus the lead paragraph, so `title:` is the frontmatter key the engine reads as note identity.

Frontmatter never enters the indexed body: `ingest.strip_frontmatter()` removes it before chunking, so frontmatter text reaches neither chunk rows nor the FTS projection, and because the wikilink graph is built from chunked body text it never sees frontmatter at all; frontmatter influences retrieval only through the separately computed doc surface.

The repo-relative posix path is the note's universal key: chunk rows and the docs lane are keyed by it, wikilink edges join on it, and a rename re-keys the existing rows for the moved path (preserving chunk ids and embeddings) instead of materializing a new note.

Callers own exactly the frontmatter keys they request: `commit_note(..., set_fields=...)` merges a caller-supplied YAML mapping (exposed over MCP as `set_fields`), and a brand-new file is rendered from that mapping alone — so a new note can legitimately carry no frontmatter block, which is how raw captures land.

The proposal queue owns no frontmatter key of its own: it either takes the free-append fast path into `commit_note` or gates each change against committed HEAD content and commits it on a proposal branch, so the frontmatter in the resulting note is exactly what the caller or generated writer supplied.

The diff-or-die frontmatter rule: a write may change only the top-level keys it explicitly requested — `changed_keys()` treats additions, removals and reordering of keys as changes, and `assert_only_changed()` raises FrontmatterDriftError carrying the offending keys and a unified diff, aborting before the file is written so a refusal leaves HEAD, the index and the audit log untouched.

Frontmatter bytes that were not requested stay byte-identical: a scalar date stays scalar rather than becoming an ISO timestamp, key order survives, and `_`-prefixed (Tolaria/Obsidian plugin) properties are preserved, because edits either rewrite only the requested scalar token in place or fall back to a round-trip-preserving YAML dump that is then diff-checked.

Wikilink graph edges come only from body `[[...]]` links: frontmatter `related_to:`/`belongs_to:` are deliberately not edges (and are never even seen, since frontmatter is stripped before chunking), self-links are dropped, and a target that does not resolve is tolerated as a dead link rather than treated as an error.

Wikilink resolution is exact and never guesses: `|display` aliases and `#anchor` fragments are stripped, the normalized path matches with or without a `.md` suffix case-insensitively, and a bare name resolves only when exactly one page shares its stem — ambiguous or missing targets return None. `Graph.resolve()` uses the same matcher, so entity resolution cannot produce a link the graph would not bind.

`build_context()` traverses both incoming and outgoing wikilink edges to a caller-supplied depth, excludes the start note from its own context, terminates on cycles, and returns a deterministic sorted path list.

`folders.derive_folders()` returns `{root, depth, folders, truncated, omitted}` where each folder entry carries `{path, writable, protected_reason, note_count}` with a recursive note count; writability is the write guard's own verdict on a synthetic `__probe__.md` placed under the prefix, so discovery cannot advertise a folder that a note write would refuse (a nested `projects/scripts/` is correctly non-writable while its parent is writable).

Folder discovery is bounded and deterministic: depth is clamped to the config-owned `LIST_FOLDERS_MAX_DEPTH` and the entry list is capped at `LIST_FOLDERS_MAX_NODES` after a sort, so truncation drops a deterministic tail and the result reports `truncated` plus an `omitted` count instead of silently losing a random subset.

Folder discovery is sanitized and index-derived: a caller-supplied `root` is normalized to a repo-relative trailing-slash prefix and an absolute path or `..` traversal is rejected with ValueError, while the path set comes from the index so skip directories (`.git`, `.hypermnesic`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.obsidian`) are structurally undiscoverable.

`config.IMMUTABLE_APPEND_ZONES` is an explicit, configuration-owned path-prefix tuple (currently `sources/`) checked by `is_immutable_append_zone`, and `propose` takes the free-append fast path only when every change is a new file absent at HEAD inside such a zone — those files are committed straight to HEAD by the gated write primitive, while an existing file in a zone or any curated path becomes a proposal branch and can never reach the fast path.

`capture` lands raw text under `sources/` through the immutable free-append fast path with no frontmatter block, defaulting to `sources/captures/<stamp>-<sha6>.md` (or the caller-supplied name) and committing it immediately, so the capture is durable without any proposal friction.

Capture triage never mutates the capture: it analyses the raw note through the read-only thinking path and emits a generated note at `dashboards/triage-<slug>.md` with `type: triage` as a proposal, carrying the observable proof that the analysis step wrote nothing and leaving the captured bytes and HEAD unchanged.

`generated.render()` marks a generated note twice: it forces `generated_by: hypermnesic` into the frontmatter and wraps the body between a visible managed-block callout (`> [!hypermnesic] generated — edits below this marker are overwritten`) and the closing marker `<!-- /hypermnesic:generated -->`, so the artifact is unmistakable even where frontmatter is collapsed; the marked region is the part regeneration overwrites.

Note kind is derived rather than registered: `generated.is_generated()` detects the `generated_by: hypermnesic` marker, and the owner-facing surfaces classify a memory as `generated`, `captured` (path under `sources/`) or `authored` — there is no enforced note-type schema behind it.

The generated review surfaces are emitted as `dashboards/`-scoped proposals with `title`, `type` and (when a timestamp is supplied) `generated_at` frontmatter: the MOC and the `.base` dashboard, the salience digest, the connection suggestions, and the daily review; the generated `.base` view config carries `generated_by` in its YAML instead of a callout.

`type:` on a generated note is descriptive metadata rather than an enforced taxonomy: no engine code reads that key, and the only frontmatter keys engine code inspects are `title:` (identity and doc surface) and the sidecar's own provenance keys inside the extraction hash gate.

No derived salience score is ever written into a source note's frontmatter: salience is scored from write-recency, link degree and embedding centrality and surfaced only in the generated digest proposal, which leaves the ranked source notes byte-identical.

A sidecar is a generated note at `sidecars/<source_rel>.md` (so `docs/report.pdf` yields `sidecars/docs/report.pdf.md`) whose frontmatter is the content-addressed provenance record: `source: sidecar`, `generated_by`, `extracted_from`, `extracted_at`, `source_sha256`, `extractor`, `extractor_version` and `_extraction_quality` with values `ok`, `partial` or `low`.

Sidecar re-extraction is hash-gated and never a silent write: a sidecar is built only when none exists, when the source hash no longer matches `source_sha256`, or when the extractor version is bumped; a changed source becomes a review-gated re-extraction proposal and the one-time cold start over a corpus is a single batched proposal rather than one pull request per file.

`sidecar.trust_tag()` is the SEC-001 untrusted-content marker: it classifies a note as `sidecar` when its path is under `sidecars/` or its frontmatter carries `source: sidecar`, and as `source` otherwise; the accepted posture keeps extracted content retrievable, and no index column stores the tag, so no query can filter on it yet.

Durable project memory routing: semantic facts, episodic/source evidence, procedural/policy rules, generated summaries citing their sources, raw captures and current-state mirrors belong in the vault, while behavioural preferences (an adjacent session/behavioural layer such as Honcho), in-flight session state, transient inferences, secrets and credentials, unreviewed sensitive material and guard-refusal workarounds do not.

Evidence-first maintenance rule: raw evidence is preserved before it is summarized — a generated summary cites source paths, labels itself generated, and never silently overwrites a raw capture; correcting or removing a source is a new git event through the memory-control preview/apply flow rather than an erasing edit.
